text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock has slid 10.65% over two weeks, with today's tiny move (-0.08%) coming after sharp drops on November 4th and 5th. The biggest driver is the sharp decline in crude oil prices: Brent crude dipped below $90 a barrel this week on optimism that the Iran conflict could end soon, and President Trump signaled he expects the situation to resolve fairly quickly. Since refiners like Marathon profit from the spread between the cost of crude oil they buy and the refined products they sell, a falling oil price narrows that profit margin—especially when the drop happens fast.

The broader headwinds are geopolitical de-escalation (which reduces oil prices) combined with a political shift against fossil fuels after the midterm elections. While refineries are running at a healthy 94.5%, the combination of lower crude prices and a regulatory environment turning more skeptical of energy production creates an uncertain outlook for the sector.
